correctness.rationale: After translation and character normalization the Fourier matrix is \(\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&\zeta\end{pmatrix}\), where character evaluation on the order-m difference runs through every m-th root of unity. Its Gram eigenvalues are \(2\pm|1+\zeta|\), so all four optimizations reduce to choosing the root nearest \(-1\). The minimum cosine distance is zero for even m and \(\sin(\pi/(2m))\) for odd m, giving every displayed formula. final_claim: For a two-point subset \(E=\{x,y\}\) of any finite abelian group, all four Ferguson--Mayeli--Sothanaphan tightness quantities depend only on \(m=\operatorname{ord}(y-x)\): the optimum is spectral exactly for even \(m\), while for odd \(m\) the exact Riesz ratio is \(\tan^2(\pi/4+\pi/(4m))\), with the corresponding stated exact L, U, and determinant formulas.
limitations: Only two-point subsets are classified; higher cardinalities and coarse-geometry lower bounds remain outside scope.
